title: The Parable Chant (Ka Phawar Pharshi)
cultural_context: Traditional didactic phawar using highland allegories (Pharshi) to teach wisdom and prudence, from 'Ka Phawar-rwai Khasi'.
lyrics_khasi:
Hoi-kiw! Sngap ko samla,
Ia ka phawar ba thoh,
Wat peit tang ia ka dur
Ba shyrkhei ha ka shnong;
U ksew uba wiar
Um ju dait ia u briew,
U sim ba kiew sha bneng
U la dei ban hiar pat.

Uba thung ia ka hok
Un kheit ia ka jingsuk,
Uba thung ia ka bamsap
Un ioh tang ka sniew;
To bat ia ka akor
Ha man ki sngi jong ka jingim,
Ba ka nam jong pha kan sah
Kum u mawkordor ba shai.
lyrics_english:
Hoi-kiw! Listen, young ones,
To the rhyming parable written,
Judge not merely by outward display
That causes a stir in the village;
The hound that barks aloud
Rarely bites the passerby,
The bird that ascends highest in sky
Must eventually alight on earth.

He who sows righteousness
Shall reap tranquility,
He who sows corruption
Shall harvest only shame;
Hold fast to good manners
All the days of your earthly life,
So that your good name endures
Like an unblemished jewel.
